decisions.reason: The indoor air quality module draws directly on the firm's established sensor, firmware and binding know-how, and demand for environmental sensing remains steady, so it stays in the portfolio.
As the latest generation of a long-running analog measurement line, it embodies the firm's accumulated knowledge and is the current reference module, so it is kept.

The MQTT proxy rests on the firm's core API-generation competence, but that same competence makes it easy to fold MQTT support into native bindings, so it carries a substantial risk of being superseded while it remains useful for now.

The CAN interface serves automation customers through the firm's communication expertise, yet its low website profile and the firm's habit of releasing improved hardware generations make replacement by a successor fairly likely.
The CO2 module fits squarely within the firm's sensor-integration knowledge and the growing demand for environmental measurement, so it is retained.
The touch panel sits further from the core module knowledge, which limits the firm's ability to refine it, but it still complements the display and prototyping kits and is kept under review.
